creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Statistics

Correlation vs Causation
Causation
Lurking Variable
Reverse Causation
description: Classification practice where students decide whether a real-world correlation is best explained by X causing Y, Y causing X, or a third variable causing both.

learningObjectives: Classify a correlation as direct causation, reverse causation, or the result of a third variable (Apply)
Identify a plausible lurking variable that could cause both variables in an association (Apply)
Explain why an observed correlation alone does not justify a causal claim (Understand)

keyQuestions: What else could explain why these two variables move together?
Which variable comes first in time?
commonMisconceptions: A strong correlation proves that one variable causes the other
The variable named first must be the cause
A third variable means the two variables are not really correlated
assessmentOpportunities: First-try score of at least 10 out of 13
Student can name the third variable before clicking Reveal Answer
Student writes a new scenario and correctly identifies its causal structure
